RE: Level 1 Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Reese Iverson
Member ID: W311137804
Reference number: POC-19FF75EFC5-13767
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-15
Requested service: ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888
Appeal deadline: 2027-02-11 (within 180 days of the notice date, as stated on the notice)

To the Appeals and Grievances Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888), as described in the notice referenced above. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria." I am requesting that Fallon Health reverse this determination and approve the requested surgery.

1. The specific criteria applied to this denial have not been disclosed to me or my surgeon.

The notice cites "the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria" but does not identify the title, policy number, or specific criteria elements that my case failed to meet. I searched Fallon Health's published Medical Policies index and located only one knee-arthroscopy-related policy, "Arthroscopic Lavage and Debridement for Osteoarthritis of the Knee." By its own terms, that policy's coverage exclusion is limited to arthroscopic lavage and debridement performed for osteoarthritis of the knee: "Fallon Health does not cover arthroscopic lavage, arthroscopic debridement, or arthroscopic lavage and debridement for the treatment of osteoarthritis of the knee because this procedure has not been shown to improve patient outcomes, specifically reduction in knee pain or improvement of knee function when compared to a control group." My case does not involve osteoarthritis of the knee (my MRI dated 2026-06-03 shows "no significant arthritis") and does not involve lavage or debridement; it involves reconstruction of a completely torn ACL. That policy therefore does not appear to apply to my request, and if it was the basis for denial, I ask that this be corrected.

I was not able to locate any other Fallon Health-published medical policy specific to ACL reconstruction or CPT 29888. I understand Fallon Health may instead apply InterQual® criteria to this procedure, as it does for other orthopedic procedures listed in its medical policy library, but that content is only accessible through a login-restricted transparency tool, and I have not been able to review it. I am not able to quote or rebut criteria I have not been permitted to see. I formally request, pursuant to my right to the specific rule, guideline, or clinical criterion relied upon in this adverse determination, that Fallon Health provide:

- The exact title, source (e.g., specific InterQual® criteria set and subset), and version/effective date of the criteria applied to this CPT 29888 request; and
- The specific criteria elements within that document that my case is alleged not to satisfy.

2. Regardless of which specific criteria were applied, my clinical record supports medical necessity for ACL reconstruction.

My treating surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has submitted documentation showing the following, which I ask the reviewer to consider in this appeal:

- Duration and severity of symptoms: 18 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest, with recurrent functional instability — the knee has given way twice while descending stairs, and I experience instability with pivoting.
- Documented failure of conservative treatment: 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy for range of motion and quadriceps strengthening with bracing (2026-04-03 through 2026-07-24, 16 completed visits, documented in the physical therapy discharge note); 8 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-18 that produced only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- Objective imaging confirmation: MRI dated 2026-06-03 showing a complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with an associated bone bruise pattern; menisci intact; no significant arthritis.
- Objective exam findings: positive provocative ligament testing on the affected side and pain-limited range of motion.
- No contraindications: no active infection, no untreated substance use disorder, BMI of 29, non-smoker.

In my own words, and without attributing this reasoning to any specific plan document I have not seen, this record demonstrates a complete, imaging-confirmed ACL tear with objective instability on examination and functional instability in daily activities, following a full and well-documented course of conservative management (structured physical therapy, bracing, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injection) that failed to resolve my symptoms. There is no evidence of advanced arthritis or other factors that would ordinarily be cited against surgical candidacy, and I have no medical contraindications to surgery.

3. Request

I ask that Fallon Health:
(a) Provide the specific medical policy or InterQual® criteria document, version, and criteria elements relied upon in the original denial;
(b) Reconsider this request in light of the clinical documentation summarized above; and
(c) Reverse the denial and authorize CPT 29888 (ACL reconstruction) as requested by Dr. Lindqvist.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-11 to be timely, and I am submitting it well in advance of that deadline. Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the address, phone number, and email listed above, and copy Dr. Lindqvist's office at [surgeon office phone/fax/address].

Enclosed/attached with this appeal:
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-15 (Reference POC-19FF75EFC5-13767)
- Physical therapy discharge summary (2026-04-03 to 2026-07-24)
- MRI report dated 2026-06-03
- Office/exam notes documenting provocative testing and instability
- Medication and injection records
- [Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Lindqvist, if separately attached]

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal. Please confirm receipt and provide the anticipated timeframe for a decision.

Sincerely,

Reese Iverson
Member ID: W311137804

cc: Dr. Lindqvist, Orthopedic Surgery, [practice name/address/fax]
